title: Zephyrine and the Prom
premise: Freya Pemberton just wants to survive senior year unnoticed at Hollowmere High, a school built over the ruins of an old manor whose 'founding families' still quietly run the town. When she's paired with Zephyrine Vale — golden girl, prom committee queen, and the last person who should notice her — for a semester project on local history, they uncover that every spring's championship and prom crown are actually rituals binding something buried beneath the gymnasium. As Freya learns her own family was one of the founding bloodlines, and Zephyrine discovers her perfect life is a gilded cage built on lies, their rivalry curdles into loyalty. To break the cycle, they must win both championships — the one everyone watches and the hidden contest of wills beneath it — before the spring equinox seals the door forever; in the end, they shatter the ritual at prom itself, choosing truth over tradition, and walk out together as the school above finally goes quiet.
about_author: Yara Ashgrove grew up in a mill town where half the buildings predated the town charter, and she never stopped wondering what was underneath them. She writes young adult stories about stubborn girls, buried histories, and the families we build when the ones we're given won't hold.

chapters.title: Head Down, Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Three weeks into Hollowmere High, Freya has perfected invisibility: perfect grades, no friends, no questions about why her family moved mid-year. But the school's odd architecture — hallways that don't align, a sealed sub-basement — keeps snagging her attention. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness, with a flicker of curiosity she can't quite smother.

chapters.title: The Pairing
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Mr. Okafor announces semester-long history projects and pairs Freya with Zephyrine Vale, who has tormented her since day one. Zephyrine protests; the teacher refuses to budge. Their first meeting in the library ends in a shouting match over topic choice until Freya mentions the sub-basement — and Zephyrine goes pale and silent. Emotional beat: hostile sparks hiding mutual recognition.

chapters.title: What Zephyrine Wants
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Behind her flawless exterior, Zeph is suffocating: her family expects her to be crowned prom queen like four generations of Vales before her. The project is her only elective freedom, and she intends to control it. She agrees to research the manor ruins only if Freya follows her lead. Emotional beat: resentment laced with envy of Freya's freedom.

chapters.title: Blueprints and Basements
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the town archive they find original manor blueprints: the school was built directly atop the old ballroom, and the gymnasium sits over something labeled only 'the Underhall.' A groundskeeper warns them off with a story about students who went missing in 1968. Emotional beat: the thrill of shared secret knowledge softening rivalry.

chapters.title: Tryouts
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya, a former competitive swimmer, is strong-armed into joining the school's championship-bound academic decathlon team by Zephyrine, who needs allies she can trust. Meanwhile the basketball team's star — Zeph's boyfriend Theo — hints that 'winning season' means more than trophies here. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging beginning to take root.

chapters.title: The Founders' List
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Researching the founding families, Zeph finds her own name among seven bloodlines sworn to 'keep the spring.' Freya recognizes Pemberton on the same list — her grandmother's maiden name. They realize the ritual isn't folklore; it's scheduled, staffed, and starring them. Emotional beat: dread braided with a strange sense of inheritance.

chapters.title: First Descent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Using a maintenance key Zeph steals from her father, they enter the Underhall: a preserved ballroom beneath the gym, cold and humming, its mirrors fogged from the inside. Something answers when Freya speaks her name aloud. They flee, but the hum follows Freya home. Emotional beat: terror transformed into complicity — now they share the secret.

chapters.title: Rival Camp
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The other founders' kids — led by immaculate Marguerite Ashcombe — notice the pair digging. Marguerite offers Freya a place among them if she drops Zeph, revealing that Zeph's friendship is transactional, part of her family's plan. Freya, burned before, almost believes it. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by an old wound reopened.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Confronted, Zeph admits her mother ordered her to befriend the Pemberton girl and keep her compliant until the equinox. Freya walks out. Alone, Zeph opens her family's locked ledger and reads what 'keeping the spring' actually requires — a Pemberton must stay. Emotional beat: guilt crystallizing into defiance of her own family.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Zeph breaks into Freya's garage at midnight with the ledger: seven families, seven obligations, and a record of every 'champion' since 1893 — each crowned, each gone by thirty. Including Freya's grandmother, listed not as escaped but as 'withheld.' Emotional beat: betrayal converted, painfully, into alliance.

chapters.title: Decathlon Prelims
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The visible championship begins. Freya leads the team to prelim victory while Zeph works the crowd like a born politician — but Marguerite's team is being fed answers from somewhere. Afterward, the Underhall's hum is louder; the school seems to know they're close to winning. Emotional beat: adrenaline shadowed by the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya's mother finally explains why they moved back: letters from Freya's grandmother, who fled Hollowmere in 1970, warn that the ritual needs a willing heir — someone who chooses to stay. Her mother came back to end it and failed. Now it wants Freya. Emotional beat: generational weight landing on one pair of shoulders.

chapters.title: Theo Knows
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Theo reveals he's known about the Underhall since freshman year; his older brother was a champion who 'moved away' and never calls. He begs Zeph to play along until graduation rather than risk everything. Torn between safety and truth, Zeph chooses Freya's side — and loses Theo. Emotional beat: the cost of loyalty made concrete.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Bargain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marguerite corners them with the full doctrine: the ritual isn't evil, it's maintenance — the thing below stays sleeping as long as it's honored, and champions are its chosen vessels. Break it, she says, and everything wakes. She offers them champion status willingly given. It's tempting precisely because it might be true. Emotional beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Semifinals and Séance
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Between semifinal rounds, the trio contacts the withheld grandmother through the Underhall's mirrors. Her message is fragmentary but clear: the vessel must consent, the crown must be accepted, and there is one night — prom, the equinox — when the door stands open both ways. Emotional beat: hope arriving hand-in-hand with a deadline.

chapters.title: The Campaign
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Prom nominations open; Zeph's family stages her coronation as inevitable. Instead, Zeph publicly declines nomination and nominates Freya, detonating her mother's plans and her social standing in one speech. The founders' kids turn on her fully. Emotional beat: exhilarating self-destruction in the name of identity.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Retaliation comes fast: Freya's decathlon eligibility is challenged, her mother's job threatened, the archive access revoked. The school itself seems to conspire — doors lock toward the Underhall, the hum enters her dreams. Marguerite warns them gently: stop, or be kept. Emotional beat: siege mentality, resolve hardening under pressure.

chapters.title: Championship Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The decathlon final: against Marguerite's suspiciously perfect team, Freya and Zeph win the visible championship fair — and in winning, feel the Underhall surge, because triumph strengthens the claim on them. That night the mirrors show them their grandmothers, young and crowned, mouthing run. Emotional beat: victory that feels like a trap closing.

chapters.title: Prom Eve
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. On the eve of the equinox, the two prepare: salt lines, the ledger, grandmother's letters, a plan to reach the ballroom's heart during prom and refuse the crown in front of all seven families. Zeph's mother finds the ledger missing and, for the first time, looks afraid — of her daughter. Emotional beat: quiet courage before the storm.

chapters.title: The Prom
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Prom unfolds as ritual: crowns presented, vows recited in archaic cadence, the floor literally breathing. When Freya is called as champion, she and Zeph speak the refusal together — and the Underhall opens beneath the gymnasium. Marguerite must choose, and chooses the girls. Emotional beat: climax — public defiance against a century of complicity.

chapters.title: What Woke and What Slept
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Below, they face not a monster but the accumulated consent of generations — and offer it something new: witness instead of worship. They read the names of every champion aloud, ending the silence that fed it. The hum becomes stillness. The door closes from the inside. Emotional beat: catharsis; grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: After the Last Dance
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Graduation approaches in a school that finally feels like just a school. Zeph's family reckons with exposure; some founders thank the girls in secret. Freya decides to stay — chosen this time — and the two, no longer nemesis or project partners, are simply each other's people. Emotional beat: found family secured; identity claimed, not assigned.
